Start Therapy

The most advanced treatment for Pigeon Toed & In-toeing and Metatarsus Adductus

UNFO is a revolutionary solution developed specifically for the therapy of Severe Metatarsus Varus, Metatarsus Adductus (Severe, Moderate, and Mild), Forefoot Adduction, and In-toeing / Pigeon toed in newborns.

UNFO addresses the difficulties and stress of frequent casting, the ineffectiveness of stretching, and the consequential under- or over-treatment of Pigeon toed / Metatarsus Adductus.

Information for parents

Common Symptom

Metatarsus Adductus (Pigeon toed / In-toeing) is a foot deformity prevalent among newly born babies. Untreated, it could lead to permanent physical damages.

Read more >

Proven Success & Clinical Trial

Standing up to the world’s highest medical standards, Thousands of parents have used the UNFO shoe and successfully treated their infants with Metatarsus Adductus (Pigeon toed / In-toeing, Forefoot Adduction) with quickly and visible results.

Read More >

Innovative Solution

MTA is treatable without the need for casting or a medical procedure. The UNFO orthopedic adjustable shoe, allows for a comfortable treatment in early stages.

Read More >

Information for professionals

Foot Deformities

The metatarsus bones are a group of five long bones that run lengthwise down the middle section of the human foot, from the toes. Metatarsus adductus (or MTA)

Read More >

Critical points

The appropriate treatment for metatarsus adductus is based on the severity of the condition, and recommended options may include observation, stretching, strapping, casting…

Read More >

UNFO design & benefits

Universal Neonatal Foot Orthotic (UNFO) is a pre-molded corrective shoe with Velcro strips that was specifically designed to treat metatarsus adductus (MTA) in newborns.

UNFO's Point of view

by Dr.Izak Daizade, MD

For every 12 live births, one infant is born with a foot defect called Metatarsus Adductus (MA). MA is known as the most common malformation in infants, most of whom are not spontaneously corrected, and require appropriate treatment and intervention.
